text: Has Minister King raised any concerns with Airservices Australia over the proposed fee increases?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The minister was concerned about what the impact on the consumer would be.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And what did you tell her?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I indicated to her that there has been a structural change in the market here in Australia post-COVID. The airlines are up-gauging their aircraft, which means they're putting in bigger aircraft. We get paid on a per-aircraft-movement basis, not on a passenger basis, and those aircraft are carrying more passengers. So we looked at the average fares being charged by the airlines and the forecast growth. For those aircraft coming in, on a per-passenger basis we're expecting about $1.50 on a one-way economy fare being the average increase per year over a five-year period. From an Airservices perspective we need to be able to invest in the infrastructure to support the industry and the growth. That funding is critical for us to be able to manage the transition of old infrastructure into new.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But the airlines don't believe that it will be only $1.50, do they?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The airlines have been engaged over an 18-month period, in the build-up to those prices—
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I am asking what their advice is of the ticket price increases.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The airlines' perspective is that ticket prices change over time. They are pointing at the moment to high fuel costs. So the last thing they need is to see further cost increases. That's the message they are giving us. The actual drivers through the regulatory model have been shared in detail with the airlines, and an ACCC independent review process is underway at the moment.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand that. So Minister King approved your request to increase air traffic control taxes?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The minister acknowledged—
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes or no?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The minister doesn't approve that. The ACCC approves it and then the processes all go to the minister for a formal approval.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But you briefed her—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We briefed her so she was aware that we were putting up a relatively steep increase and the reasons why.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And she was okay with that?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: She was comfortable with us to progress the consultation process with the airlines and to commence the ACCC process.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: She wasn't very happy with the spate of delays and near misses. She called you in for a meeting on 10 August and she reported that you had committed to implement improved rostering practices from early September. So what improved rostering practices have you implemented since that meeting?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'll pass to Mr Curran to talk to the detail on rostering.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We've put in place a new roster as at 1 September in Sydney tower, which gave us some more options around the way we were deploying our staff.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So what changed?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We also were able to deploy some of the staff who were deployed elsewhere in the Sydney basin, and who had previously worked at Kingsford Smith, back to Kingsford Smith, and that gave us some additional resources.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How many?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There was a total of four FTE—full time equivalent—that we were able to move back on a temporary basis.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So the only change you made to rostering practices as a result of the minister calling you in was to get four FTEs back into the Sydney tower?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. I'll step through a few—
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We're on limited time, and I know that verbose answers are your specialty. Let's just cut to the chase.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We're going to place some significant investment around our training program. In particular, we've acquired an additional simulator for Sydney tower so we have two simulators to do more training downstairs in situ in Sydney, which increases the throughput. There are limits on how many people you can train in a control tower at any given time. That allows us to take more training downstairs and less on the job potentially.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, and when is that—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The first simulator has been implemented. The second simulator is in situ being set up now. It will be operational for the first course next year.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. I want to understand why you had to wait to be hauled in to the minister to get the four FTE back in and why you couldn't have just done that immediately after 10 August.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think it's fair to say that some of the challenges we had in July and August had us looking at some of our deployment practices and we were working toward some of these changes.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What was wrong with your deployment practices?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: With regard to where we had staff—
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Where did you have them?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They were deployed to Western Sydney airport.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Where nobody was taking off or landing?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not during the day, but at nighttime; that's right.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: With the freight flights.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's correct, yes.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How many freight flights at Western Sydney airport?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Monday to Friday, approximately 20 to 25 per night.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So the four you have taken out of Western Sydney airport you have put back into Kingsford Smith on a temporary basis.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Practically we were able to use people between the two locations, so they maintained their recency, their currency, in both locations.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So they're not location-dependent?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They were able to work between both locations.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In the period following the meeting with Minister King, a further three near-miss events occurred at Sydney airport. The report released by the ATSB today indicates an air traffic control operator in the tower with a high predicted fatigue level during the 17 August near-miss incident. Would that controller have been in the tower under the improved rostering practices implemented in September?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: All of the rostering practices affect all staff in Kingsford Smith tower, so the answer is yes.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On 30 September the minister announced the establishment of the Sydney Airport Air Traffic Control Independent Assurance Panel. Whose idea was it to establish the panel? Were you consulted on its establishment?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, we were consulted on that. I was looking at a scenario where we could have some independence to give the board some comfort around the work that management was doing. At the same time, the department and minister were also looking for an option to provide that independence. So we had some input to that process, but ultimately it sits with the department and the minister.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Who brought the idea to who?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I briefed the department on the concept I had for briefing airport and then the conversation commenced from there.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So what does the panel do on a day-to-day basis? Does it interact with ASA management?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The ministerial-appointed panel has a terms of reference that was agreed with the department and the minister; it has a very specific brief. It will review those incidents, it will review the ATSB reports, and the CASA review that's underway. Its members will also do their own assurance activity in terms of interviewing. The actual terms of reference you would need to talk to the department specifically about, but at a high level that's the nature of the activities.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So was the terms of reference for the panel agreed with Airservices Australia as well?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We had input to it, but it was really driven by the department and the minister.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The terms of reference?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So let me get this right: the minister does the right thing, hauls you in and you're now claiming credit for the panel getting set up.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm not claiming that.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I asked whose bright idea it was—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I raised the concept for the board and then there was a conversation more broadly around independent review. I'm not taking credit for it. I was talking specifically to the process.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Where the bright idea came for Airservices Australia, or anyway, the concept. Does the panel report directly to the minister? If so, how frequently?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: My understanding is that it reports there. It's a matter for the department because the department is managing the day-to-day contracts. We have as yet to meet with them. Mr Curran and I are meeting with them later this week so we'll have a bit more insight as to how the assurance panel is proposing to approach these objectives.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Does the reporting for the assurance panel go to the minister with noting to ASA, or how do you envisage the reporting of the panel to roll out?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Given that it is with the department, I'm sure there will be a draft report at the end that we would be consulted on. When I say, 'consulted on', similar to ATSB or a CASA review, we would provide any commentary typically around actions, omissions or errors that might be in there. Then that will be shared with the board of Airservices.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What is the budget for the panel over its first six months?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You would have to refer to the department. I haven't been involved in that process.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So it is not being funded by Airservices Australia?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How many international controllers have been hired in the last three years who did not get rated to operate here?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'll pass to Mr Curran.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have had 48 international air traffic controllers recruited in the last several years but I don't have the details of the pass or failure rate. That's something we would have to take on notice. Typically, when an international recruit moves to Australia, if they were to go to a location and their first attempt does not work out, we would look to understand where the deficiencies were in that particular location and understand if we could find a better match for them prior to terminating their employment.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Forty-eight international controllers is a big amount of people power to help you do your job, and you don't know what the pass or fail rate is?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's just that we haven't broken it down for that particular cohort on the data sets that I have here, unless Ms Mesa can provide that information.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, I can. The data that I have averaged out shows that the international experienced controllers' pass rate is sitting at around 85 per cent.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So of the 48, we should have—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Eighty-five per cent of those.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. Is that the case?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Again, to Mr Curran's point, I haven't got the data in relation to that period of time specifically by what location.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It is incredible that you don't keep that type of data.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We do keep that data.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm looking at my data tables on that one.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No—
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It is 48 in total.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: For the last couple of years, yes.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. So you have 41 international and 0.33 recurring. Is that correct?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Based on those calculations, I would say yes.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is that number included in the 95, Mr Sharp?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The 95 of the total recruits for this calendar year, of which—
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: With the 95 for this calendar year—remember that Airservices Australia was crowing that you have 170, but it was 95. Of that 95, 41 are internationals; is that correct?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The 48 number that I think you were talking about is for the last three years; is that correct, Mr Curran?
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think Mr Curran was being as specific as three years. I'd love to know over how many years.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The 95 number is the 95 pass rate. That's how many air traffic controllers into the Australian system this year we expect to pass. portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Of the 95 that you expect to pass, what proportion of those are international operators?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't have that data to hand; perhaps Ms Mesa does. If not, we can take it on notice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

In the Sydney terminal control unit—the other part of the puzzle of Sydney air traffic control is the airspace management, as well as the aerodrome management at Kingsford Smith—we have a very good pass rate in the terminal control unit. Sydney tower has been the challenge for us.
witness_position: Deputy Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That is the understatement of the year. What vetting was done when hiring international recruits? What happens?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. Of the pass rate, for those who did not pass, they would have returned back to their home country.
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Out of the 48, how many people actually hired stayed on?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: To the point of the pass rate of that—
witness_position: Chief People and Culture Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I don't want to know the pass rate. I want your evidence as to how many people, how many individuals, are now on Airservices Australia's books from this program of international controllers?

text: Going to Mr Curran's point, we'll have to take that on notice and make sure that we furnish you with that specific detail.

I want to go back to a question I asked at the October estimates last year, question on notice SQ25-002063, which was in relation to impact of aircraft emissions on water supplies. In the conversation, I was told that there were some international studies available. The answer to the question on notice referred to chapter 13 of the Western Sydney EIS, volume 4, appendix G of the Community Health Western Sydney Airport EIS 2016, technical paper 12, volume D, Airspace Aircraft Emissions, Brisbane New Parallel Runway EIS. But when I go to chapter 13 of the Sydney EIS, which is the human health element, none of those, I have to say, are what I would regard as a study; they basically state conclusions, which is what the Sydney EIS does. I will quote from chapter 13:

The water quality health risk assessment found that potential impacts to Sydney's drinking water supplies, in reservoirs at Warragamba and Prospect, is unlikely due to their distance from the airport site and low predicted levels of particulates at those locations.

That's a distance issue. It continued:

Similarly, the health risk assessment did not find evidence to suggest that private rainwater tanks would be adversely affected by airport operations. Comprehensive surface and groundwater baseline data will be collected throughout the construction and operation of the Stage 1 development—

which is what I assume we are going into now—

to better inform the future assessment of potential water contamination.

That says to me that you don't actually know. I would be very curious to see, firstly, the international studies that you talked about when we discussed it. I am happy for you to take these questions on notice. Is the health risk assessment referred to here a public document?

text: What do Nauru Airlines' CASA-approved procedures require, if anything, when Nauru International Airport rescue and firefighting category falls below what's required for an aircraft type? portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: If it were a major defect, it would be reported to CASA, it being an Australian registered aircraft.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: The representatives of the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility are appearing via videoconference. Does anyone want to make a very brief opening statement before we go to questions?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Senator McDonald.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It is exciting to not only see you this evening but see you early. It's a red-letter day for the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility. Mr MacDonald, I want to start by asking you about the recent report tabled by the Joint Standing Committee on Northern Australia. I am going to assume that you have read that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's right. It came in last week.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It talks about a lack of coordination between the Commonwealth, state and territory governments and local councils as a barrier to development across Northern Australia. Has NAIF seen evidence that the report's findings of a lack of coordination between the Commonwealth, state and territory governments and local council are a barrier to development across Northern Australia?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you for the question. We engage regularly at Commonwealth and state levels. We have a regular dialogue with the jurisdictions. We speak regularly with the Commonwealth and we engage with them to try to make sure that we can deliver infrastructure outcomes for Northern Australia. We see very positive dialogue. We would welcome the opportunity to do more and engage more at both a state and council level.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You're telling me that approvals are fast and predictable, that projects are screaming out the door because it's all working seamlessly?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There are certainly challenges for projects in the north, as there are challenges with projects everywhere. We see a lot of opportunity, and we are very keen to play a key role in helping to facilitate those projects.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Has NAIF seen any projects in its pipeline that have been delayed or had their costs increased, or even had projects not proceed because of poor coordination between different levels of government?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We've had projects that haven't proceeded. I wouldn't say that's because of poor coordination. As I said, in our engagement, at both a state and council level, we have good engagement. We spend a lot of time working with different stakeholders, to give our projects the best chance of success.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's not the engagement; it's whether or not the projects are being approved in a timely manner to go ahead and be successful.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, but I think your question was specifically whether that was due to a lack of coordination. There are definitely projects that have not proceeded as fast as we or the proponents may have liked. I haven't seen evidence that is due to a lack of coordination.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What about project approvals?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Approvals on all projects take time. We have seen some where those have taken longer than we would like, but we continue to work with proponents and talk to the jurisdictions to ensure that those approvals are provided as soon as possible.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: This is what I am seeking to understand. You have provided finance. The proponent is burning money. I'm trying to get clarity around the sense of whether or not we are getting projects through the 'valley of death', through the approvals process, through finance approvals, through first cashflow, first project milestones, in a way that allows them to be successful. You are telling me, though, that approvals are not a problem, that there are no problems in Northern Australia and that I've got it completely wrong.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: May I clarify my comment? I was saying that there are projects that are taking time to get approvals. That doesn't, from what I've seen, appear to be due to a lack of coordination. We would definitely like more projects to be advanced. That's what NAIF is here for. We see our key role as funding economic infrastructure in Northern Australia. It's something we're very passionate about. We do see that some projects are delayed and there are some challenges to some projects proceeding. Your question was whether that was due to a lack of coordination. I was saying that it's not due to a lack of coordination; in our experience, it's due to the fact that these projects are complex and they take time. At times the approval process can be quite long.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The Minister for Northern Australia has secured an additional $2 billion of funding for NAIF. Your mandate is to get money out of the door to projects, in order to get them completed, but you have another agency that's not completing approvals in an economically efficient way. What else would you call that, apart from a lack of coordination?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think the projects that we support are subject to a number of approvals. Sometimes that's at the Commonwealth level with, for example, EPBC approvals. At times, that's at the state level, such as with development approvals. So there's a range of approvals on projects and the approvals process is very thorough, so sometimes it takes time.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand that. But this is the point, isn't it? With the Northern Australia agenda, we have an agency giving them money and other agencies that are slow in the way that they do approvals. It is also cross-jurisdictional, so you might have the state and the feds doing approvals. Meanwhile, the money that you've loaned them, their cash flow, is being depleted on salaries, people, redoing approvals and whatever else rather than starting to commence the project, which potentially will threaten the project viability. I think there's a lack of urgency from all agencies, which means that, with these projects, we're spending money on things on which we shouldn't have to spend money. And who misses out? It's the people of Northern Australia, who don't get a project built in a timely manner or jobs on the ground, with whatever the product is that you're going to build.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand. I can certainly assure you that NAIF, as an organisation, is very committed to timely approvals and making sure that we can deploy our capital as fast as possible. We do understand that it's the deployment of capital that helps to support economic growth, jobs and Indigenous outcomes, which is the reason that we exist.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can you give me a specific example of a project where delayed approvals have delayed a project or affected its viability?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can give you one example: the Townsville affordable living project. We made an investment decision on that in the last financial year, 2025-26. We were very keen to support that project because it's social and affordable housing. It didn't receive the development approval that it needed and so, at this stage, that project is not proceeding.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On that, I note that there are two housing projects: student accommodation in Darwin and the social housing project in Townsville. Given that we have a housing fund, do you think this is still within the remit of what NAIF was established for, for Northern Australia?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As you're aware, NAIF was set up to fund economic infrastructure in Northern Australia that delivers growth, jobs and Indigenous outcomes. Housing has emerged as a key constraint on economic growth in the north, in terms of being able to house essential workers and build communities. So we are supporting housing projects wherever we can, particularly in the social and affordable housing space, to best support the development of Northern Australia.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So social housing is to provide a project workforce made up of people who would otherwise not be paid enough to be able to finance their own home. Is that right?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We're using social and affordable housing as an area that we are very focused on. I think housing, more broadly, is a challenge in Northern Australia, as it also is in other regions. In the north, we need housing to support workers and communities, so that is something that we are helping to support.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Given that the Commonwealth has a housing infrastructure fund, I'm just not certain that this is a remit for the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. We have worked very closely with Housing Australia on the projects that we've been involved in, and we work very closely with them on these housing projects.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What about the Cairns Seniors Community Housing Project? What assessment did NAIF undertake originally to determine that the project would not proceed without its financial assistance?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I might hand over in a moment to two of my colleagues who are here: Stephen Land, our Chief Investment Officer, whose team was involved in putting the deal together; and Raveen Sritharan, our Chief Risk Officer. That is a project that we have been involved in, and we're very proud of our involvement. Raveen, who will speak in a moment, visited the project just last week. I might hand over to Stephen first so that he can answer your first question, and Raveen can follow on.
witness_position: Chief Executive Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The Cairns housing project is a challenging project. As you're aware, the market in Northern Australia is materially different from the market in southern Australia. We spoke with Housing Australia about the project initially. To get the project built to a budget that was acceptable, in order to access not only the Queensland government's operating support but also the Housing Australia subsidy, it was identified that it would need to be produced on a prefabricated basis, and that was something that the Housing Australia investment team was not comfortable with. So we actually took that project forward with a prefabricated model, and it's being delivered in a phased approach. The structure is that we're working with a commercial bank around the delivery of the actual project on a construction basis. Housing Australia will then join the project post completion, once that risk around the prefabrication piece has been mitigated through the construction. It's very much a case of being fit for purpose for Northern Australia. There was close collaboration with Housing Australia, but we have a different mandate. Our mandate is very much around delivering higher risk projects in Northern Australia, recognising that construction costs and delivery timelines et cetera are challenged versus, I guess, the broader experience in southern Australia.

text: Oh, Victoria. Your reputation remains. That, I thought, was a surprising decision, given the rainfall and other issues, but it turned out to be the case.
